title: Specific Technique for Assessing Fall Risk in Home Environment
recommendation_text: Conduct a structured home safety assessment focusing on these specific areas: 1) Lighting - check for adequate illumination in hallways, stairways, and bathrooms 2) Flooring - identify loose rugs, uneven surfaces, and clutter 3) Bathroom - assess need for grab bars, non-slip mats, and raised toilet seats 4) Stairs - check for secure handrails and contrast marking on steps. Document findings and implement targeted modifications.
implementation_guidance: Use a standardized home safety checklist. Take photos (with permission) to document hazards. Prioritize modifications based on risk level and patient preferences. Provide written recommendations and follow up within 30 days to assess implementation.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 3-5 modifiable fall risk factors per home, 30-40% reduction in falls with implementation of recommended modifications, and increased patient confidence in home safety.
target_population: Older adults, individuals with mobility impairments, and those with history of falls
cost_effectiveness: Moderate-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing fall-related injuries and hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Gillespie LD, Robertson MC, Gillespie WJ, et al.
citation_title: Interventions for preventing falls in older people living in the community

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Parkinson's Disease
recommendation_text: Ask patients with Parkinson's disease these specific questions about medication timing: 1) 'How often do you take your Parkinson's medication exactly as prescribed?' 2) 'Do you ever delay or skip doses because of side effects?' 3) 'Do you notice your symptoms returning before your next scheduled dose?' 4) 'What system do you use to remember your medication times?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reviews. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific adherence patterns and motor fluctuations. Consider medication timing adjustments or extended-release formulations for patients with wearing-off symptoms.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of suboptimal medication timing, 20-30% reduction in off-time, and improved quality of life scores.
target_population: Patients with Parkinson's disease on dopaminergic medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for improving symptom control and quality of life.
citation_title: Effect of educational intervention on medication timing in Parkinson's disease: a randomized controlled trial

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Transplant Recipients
recommendation_text: Implement the 'BATHE' technique during medication reviews: B (Background) - 'How have things been going with your medications?' A (Affect) - 'How do you feel about taking these medications long-term?' T (Trouble) - 'What troubles you most about your medication regimen?' H (Handling) - 'How are you handling these challenges?' E (Empathy) - Express understanding and validate concerns. Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement at each follow-up visit. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop clear protocols for addressing identified adherence barriers. Consider electronic monitoring for high-risk patients.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of psychosocial barriers to adherence, 25-30% improvement in immunosuppressant adherence rates, and reduced rejection episodes.
target_population: Solid organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing costly rejection episodes and graft failure.
citation_authors: De Geest S, Dobbels F, Fluri C, et al.
citation_title: Adherence to the therapeutic regimen in heart, lung, and heart-lung transplant recipients

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Cognitive Function in Primary Care
recommendation_text: Administer the Mini-Cog assessment by following these specific steps: 1) Ask the patient to repeat three unrelated words (e.g., banana, sunrise, chair) 2) Ask the patient to draw a clock showing 11:10 3) Ask the patient to recall the three words. Score 1 point for each word recalled and 2 points for a normal clock. Implement cognitive evaluation for scores ≤3.
implementation_guidance: Administer annually for patients 65+ or when cognitive concerns are reported. Use consistent word sets and scoring criteria. Document scores and observations in a dedicated section of the EHR. Develop referral pathways for abnormal results.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 15-20% more cases of mild cognitive impairment, earlier intervention and support, and improved care planning.
target_population: Adults 65+ and younger patients with cognitive complaints or risk factors
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening (under $5 per patient) with potential for significant impact on care planning and caregiver support.
citation_authors: Borson S, Scanlan JM, Chen P, et al.
citation_title: The Mini-Cog as a screen for dementia: validation in a population-based sample
citation_journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Glaucoma
recommendation_text: Ask patients with glaucoma these specific questions about eye drop administration: 1) 'Can you show me how you put in your eye drops?' 2) 'How often do you miss putting in your eye drops?' 3) 'What difficulties do you have with your eye drops?' 4) 'Do you ever run out of eye drops before your next refill?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Have placebo drops available for technique demonstration. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider eye drop aids for patients with dexterity issues.
expected_outcomes: Identification of technique errors in 50-60% of patients, 20-30% improvement in adherence rates, and better intraocular pressure control.
target_population: Patients with glaucoma on topical medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing disease progression and vision loss.
citation_authors: Newman-Casey PA, Weizer JS, Heisler M, et al.
citation_title: Systematic review of educational interventions to improve glaucoma medication adherence

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
recommendation_text: Use the 'Ask-Tell-Ask' technique for medication counseling: 1) Ask - 'What do you know about how your IBD medications work?' 2) Tell - provide targeted information to address knowledge gaps 3) Ask - 'What questions do you have about your treatment plan?' For patients with adherence concerns, implement medication reminder systems tailored to their daily routine.
implementation_guidance: Implement during initial prescription and reinforce at follow-up visits. Document specific knowledge gaps identified and education provided. Consider electronic reminders or mobile apps for patients with busy schedules.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient knowledge of IBD medications, 25-30% improvement in adherence rates, and reduced disease flares.
target_population: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease on maintenance therapy
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing hospitalizations and complications.
citation_authors: Jackson CA, Clatworthy J, Robinson A, et al.
citation_title: Factors associated with non-adherence to oral medication for inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Older Adults
recommendation_text: Use the 'brown bag' medication review by asking patients to bring all medications (prescription, over-the-counter, supplements) to the visit in their original containers. Compare with the medication list by asking: 1) 'How do you organize your medications?' 2) 'What time of day do you take each medication?' 3) 'Which medications do you find most difficult to take as prescribed?' Document discrepancies and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Send medication bag reminder before appointments. Allocate 15-20 minutes for comprehensive review. Document specific adherence barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider medication simplification for complex regimens.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 2-3 medication discrepancies per patient, 20-25% improvement in adherence rates, and reduced adverse drug events.
target_population: Older adults taking multiple medications (5 or more)
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing medication-related hospitalizations.
citation_title: Managing medications in clinically complex elders: 'There's got to be a happy medium'

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Osteoporosis
recommendation_text: Ask patients on osteoporosis medications these specific questions: 1) 'What time of day do you take your bone medication?' 2) 'How long do you wait before eating or lying down after taking it?' 3) 'How often do you miss doses?' 4) 'What side effects have you experienced?' Document responses and provide targeted education to address misconceptions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reviews. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific adherence patterns and barriers. Provide written instructions for proper administration of bisphosphonates.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of administration errors, 20-25% improvement in adherence rates, and better bone mineral density outcomes.
target_population: Patients on oral bisphosphonates or other osteoporosis medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing fractures and associated costs.
citation_authors: Kothawala P, Badamgarav E, Ryu S, et al.
citation_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of real-world adherence to drug therapy for osteoporosis

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in COPD
recommendation_text: Implement the 'Teach-to-Goal' method for inhaler technique: 1) Demonstrate correct technique 2) Ask patient to demonstrate back 3) Identify and correct errors 4) Ask patient to demonstrate again 5) Repeat until perfect technique is achieved. Document number of rounds needed to achieve mastery and reassess at each visit.
implementation_guidance: Implement at initiation of therapy and reassess at each follow-up visit. Keep placebo inhalers for all prescribed devices. Document specific errors observed and corrections provided. Consider spacer devices for patients with persistent coordination issues.
expected_outcomes: Improved inhaler technique in 80-90% of patients, 25-30% improvement in medication adherence, and reduced COPD exacerbations.
target_population: Patients with COPD using inhaled medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing emergency department visits and hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Press VG, Arora VM, Shah LM, et al.
citation_title: Teach-to-Goal for Inhaler Use in Inpatients with Asthma or COPD

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Rheumatoid Arthritis
recommendation_text: Use the 'DMARD Adherence Questionnaire' by asking: 1) 'In the past month, have you ever forgotten to take your arthritis medication?' 2) 'Do you sometimes stop taking your medication when you feel better?' 3) 'Do you sometimes stop taking your medication when you feel worse?' 4) 'Did you take your arthritis medication yesterday?' Score 1 point for each 'yes' to questions 1-3 or 'no' to question 4. Implement adherence intervention for scores ≥1.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider medication calendar or mobile app reminders for patients with memory-related non-adherence.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30-40% more patients with adherence issues, improved disease activity scores, and reduced disease progression.
target_population: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis on disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs)
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for improving treatment outcomes and preventing disability.
citation_authors: de Klerk E, van der Heijde D, Landewé R, et al.
citation_title: Patient compliance in rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, and gout
